base.$description: App background behind everything. True black on OLED in dark mode (neutral/100); warm paper in light.

canvas.$description: The working canvas — a model, a map, a photo, a game board. True black in dark mode, so the content is the brightest thing on screen.

raised.$description: Sheets, cards, lists and banners — the one raised layer. Flat: separated by border.subtle, not by shadow.

control.$description: Controls, floating panels, fields and chips. Dark elevation builds up from black: 100 → 90 → 80.

scrim.$description: Dimming layer under modal sheets (64 % black). Decorative; not a contrast pair.

tertiary.$description: Placeholder and hint text. Still AA on every surface.

disabled.$description: Disabled labels. Exempt from WCAG contrast; always paired with a disabled shape/state.

subtle.$description: Dividers, card and banner outlines. Decorative (no contrast requirement); flat surfaces separate with this instead of shadow.

strong.$description: Field outlines and control boundaries that identify a control — 3:1 non-text contrast.

fill.$description: The accent, strictly: the active control, a selected chip or segment, a toggle that is on. Never decoration, links, headings, brand marks or a primary button.

fill-pressed.$description: Pressed state of an accent fill.

on.$description: Label/icon on an accent fill (dark text on amber).

text.$description: The accent as text or an icon on a surface: the label of the active control or selected segment only. Links are neutral (underlined).

focus.$description: Keyboard / Full Keyboard Access focus ring (2 px, offset 2 px).

primary-fill.$description: Primary button fill (Beatham convention: neutral/20 fill, neutral/80 label in dark). Neutral, so the accent never competes with it.

destructive-label.$description: Destructive button label (always with a trash or xmark glyph). One step lighter than error in dark so it reads on controls.

stroke.$description: Outline of the selected object (a shape, an edge, a card on a canvas).

fill.$description: Selected tint (brand/50 at 24 %). The only tint in the chrome; decorative — the stroke carries the contrast.

hover.$description: Pre-selection (touch-down / pointer hover) outline. Thinner than the selection stroke; in light mode it shares the stroke colour and differs by weight.

signal.$description: State colours for marks, glyphs and short labels. Always with a glyph and a label — never colour alone. Two hues in the chrome by default (blue, red); green only for results a person checks. Sub-brands map their product states onto these (brand/rules.json).

info.$description: Blue (Callout): still open, still free, in progress — something you may still change. Pair with an open glyph and a count or label.

negative.$description: Red (Negative): broken — an error, a conflict, a failed result, a destructive outcome. Pair with ✕ or an exclamation glyph.

caution.$description: Light red: about to go wrong — a warning. A lighter step of the same red as negative, with ⚠; told apart by step and glyph, never by colour alone.

positive.$description: Green (Success): a result that passed a check. Results only — never “saved” or “sent”, which stay neutral. With ✓ and a label.

error.$description: Error text/icon with the xmark glyph (✕): full red. Name the thing, the reason and the fix.

error-surface.$description: Error banner: flat — the raised surface with a border; the glyph and title carry the red.

warning.$description: UI warning text/icon with the triangle glyph (⚠): a lighter red step than error — told apart from errors by step and glyph, never by colour alone.

success.$description: Success text/icon with the checkmark glyph: neutral in the chrome (saved, sent, exported). Green is reserved for signal.positive results.

info.$description: Informational text/icon with the info glyph: neutral.
